stages.fix_analysis: The fix (f37815b323) adds isPersistentBrowserProfileMutation() guard to browser.request handler, blocking POST /profiles/create and DELETE /profiles/<name> routes. This is a proper authorization fix for CWE-863.
stages.bic_trace: The vulnerable code was introduced in e7fdccce39 (Jan 27, 2026) by Peter Steinberger, which created the browser.request gateway handler without route-level authorization filtering. The scope assignment (browser.request under WRITE_SCOPE instead of ADMIN_SCOPE) was formalized in a40c10d3e2 (Feb 19, 2026) by the same author.
stages.ai_signal_check: No AI co-author trailers, bot authorship, or AI-generated patterns found on either vulnerability-introducing commit (e7fdccce39, a40c10d3e2). Author Peter Steinberger is the project's primary human maintainer with thousands of commits. Pipeline found AI signals (Claude Opus 4.5/4.6 co-author trailers) on 2 unrelated BICs at blame_confidence 0.27, but these are for files (payloads.ts, exec-approvals.ts) completely unrelated to the browser.request authorization bypass.
stages.causality: Classic human design oversight: a large 91-file refactoring (e7fdccce39) created a proxy handler that forwarded all browser routes without filtering admin-only operations. The code existed and was exploitable from Jan 27, 2026 until the fix on Mar 12, 2026.

root_cause: The pipeline correctly identified this as NOT_AI (ai_confidence: 0.0). However, the pipeline identified 20 fix commits via advisory_version source (entire version diff between affected and patched releases) instead of narrowing to the specific security fix commit f37815b323. This caused blame to scatter across many unrelated files. The core vulnerability-introducing commit (e7fdccce39) was never identified as a BIC by the pipeline.
improvement_suggestions: Fix commit resolution from advisory_version diffs should filter to security-relevant commits rather than including all commits between affected and patched versions
For large version-diff fix sets (20 commits), the pipeline should attempt to identify the specific security fix by matching CVE description keywords against commit messages and changelogs
The CHANGELOG.md entry explicitly references GHSA-vmhq-cqm9-6p7q - this could be used to narrow from 20 fix commits to the 1 relevant one
